data.long_meaning: Rajas is a Sanskrit word meaning 'red' and 'passionate'. It is also the name of one of the three gunas, or qualities, in Hinduism, representing activity, motion, and passion. The name is associated with the sun and with kings and rulers. The name Rajas carries the meaning “King, Sun, Red, Passion” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Rajas usually hope their child will grow to embody king, sun, red, passion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the active, moving principle in the universe, and is one of the three gunas in Hinduism. It is also associated with the sun, and with the qualities of passion, desire, and action.

data.cultural_impact: The name Rajas carries a powerful cultural significance as it is associated with strength, leadership, and passion. In Hindu mythology, the gods Indra and Agni, representing power and fire, respectively, are often referred to as Rajas. The name is also indicative of a dynamic, energetic, and charismatic personality – traits that have been valued in Hindu society for centuries. The association of the name with rulers and kings also highlights the importance of leadership and strong, decisive action in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, Rajas is one of the three gunas that influence the behavior and evolution of all beings. It represents desire, attachment, and passion. While Rajas energy can be a source of inspiration, creativity, and motivation, it can also lead to suffering, bondage, and illusion. The spiritual significance of the name Rajas lies in the reminder to balance the desire and passion with detachment and inner peace, leading to greater self-awareness and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Rajas symbolizes passion, action, and creativity. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'rajas,' which means 'mode of matter' or 'passionate attachment.' In Hinduism, it is one of the three gunas or qualities of the universe, representing the dynamic and active principle.
